original_question: Does there exist a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow is completely integrable?
target_in_paper: Question 10.1.1 (Bangert) in §10.1, “Metrics with integrable geodesic flow on surfaces of genus ≥ 2.” ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official target almost verbatim: it asks for the existence of a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow is completely integrable. So the object class, topology, genus range, and dynamical property are all correct. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places this specifically in §10.1, under “Integrability and ergodicity of geodesic flows on surfaces of higher genus”; a fully stand-alone version should preserve that exact scope, namely a connected closed surface of genus at least 2. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
The paper explicitly notes that the answer may depend on the smoothness/regularity class of the metric; your draft does not mention this caveat. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The phrase “completely integrable” is not fixed once and for all in the paper. The immediately following sentence distinguishes two intended strengths: an additional first integral functionally independent of the Hamiltonian on an open everywhere dense subset, or the stronger requirement that this subset have full measure. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

To be fully self-contained, one should make explicit that the geodesic flow is being viewed in its Hamiltonian form: the paper’s notation section defines the geodesic flow φ_t, while Question 10.1.1 discusses an integral independent of the Hamiltonian. On a surface, this means one extra first integral besides the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

One should not silently narrow the problem to polynomial-in-velocities integrals. The nearby discussion in §10.2 explains that for genus ≥ 2 surfaces, additional integrals polynomial in velocities and functionally independent of the energy are already ruled out, so Question 10.1.1 is broader than that separate polynomial-integral problem. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist a connected closed surface M of genus g(M) ≥ 2 and a Riemannian metric g on M such that the geodesic flow of g is completely integrable, in the sense that the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian admits an additional first integral functionally independent of it on an open everywhere dense subset of phase space (or, in the stronger interpretation explicitly noted in the paper, on a full-measure subset)? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact official problem in the paper: Question 10.1.1 in §10.1. The neighboring Question 10.1.2 (zero Liouville entropy) is presented only as an easier version, not as an equivalent reformulation, and Question 10.1.3 is merely related through the construction of an integral from a second metric. I therefore kept the statement at Question 10.1.1 and only imported the paper’s own clarifications about what “completely integrable” may mean, while avoiding any shift to weaker entropy questions, Finsler/projective-equivalence questions, or polynomial-integral variants. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
